question: A 34-year-old man consulted for fever and malaise. In the clinical history, homosexual relationships were collected for 4 months with a new partner. 2 months before the current consultation, she had an ulcerous lesion on the glans, painless, with bilateral inguinal adenopathies, all self-limiting. Serological studies are requested with the following results: HIV negative, RPR 1/320, TPHA 1/128. What treatment would you indicate in this patient?

options.opb: Intravenous penicillin G, 24 MU every day for 14 days.
options.opc: Penicillin Benzatine 2.4 MU intramuscular, three doses in three consecutive weeks.
options.opd: Ceftriaxone 2 grams intramuscular in a single dose.
options.ope: Penicillin Benzatine 2.4 MU intramuscular in a single dose.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Patient presents with fever and malaise" -> "History of ulcerous lesion on glans" -> "Bilateral inguinal adenopathies noted" -> "Serological results show RPR 1/320" -> "Indicates possible syphilis infection" -> "TPHA 1/128 confirms syphilis diagnosis" -> "Treatment for syphilis recommended" -> "Penicillin Benzathine 2.4 MU intramuscular in a single dose is standard for early syphilis" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Patient has fever and malaise" -> "Recent sexual history suggests risk for STIs" -> "Painless ulcer on glans suggests primary syphilis" -> "RPR and TPHA results indicate syphilis" -> "Guidelines recommend treatment with Benzathine penicillin" -> "Single dose of Penicillin Benzathine 2.4 MU is effective" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Patient reports fever and malaise" -> "History of ulcerative lesion and adenopathy" -> "RPR and TPHA results indicate syphilis" -> "Standard treatment for syphilis is penicillin" -> "Benzathine penicillin is preferred for early syphilis" -> "Single dose is effective for treatment" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Patient has fever and malaise" -> "Ulcerous lesion and adenopathy suggest syphilis" -> "RPR and TPHA confirm syphilis diagnosis" -> "Treatment options include various penicillin regimens" -> "Benzathine penicillin is commonly used" -> "Single dose is less effective than multiple doses" -> "Consider three doses for optimal treatment" -> 80%
analysis: The patient presents with a history suggestive of primary syphilis, indicated by the painless ulcer on the glans and the serological results showing a positive RPR and TPHA. The appropriate treatment for primary syphilis is Benzathine penicillin G, typically administered as a single dose of 2.4 million units intramuscularly. Therefore, the best option is to provide Penicillin Benzathine in a single dose.
